question: Perform peptide identification on the provided DDA mzML file using the given FASTA database and report peptide-spectrum matches.

files.eval_guideline: The set of (spectrum_id, peptide_sequence, charge) tuples must match the reference; protein_accession may differ for shared peptides; modification notation must be present and consistent.
files.match_reasoning: The filenames are identical and both are TSV files containing Comet PSM output for BSA2_F1.

parameters.question: Compare Comet PSM tables from DDA peptide identification of BSA2_F1.mzML. The set of (spectrum_id, peptide_sequence, charge) tuples must match the reference; protein_accession may differ for shared peptides; modification notation must be present and consistent. Row/column order may differ.

files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline asks for a record-level match on (spectrum_id, peptide_sequence, charge) tuples, and the database search is deterministic. Approximate matching handles differences in row and column order and allows protein accessions to vary for shared peptides.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables are long-format PSM lists with one row per match, so no transpose is needed. All four reference columns have candidate columns with the same name. The 14 extra candidate columns (scores, masses, retention time, etc.) are left out. The evaluation compares the set of (spectrum_id, peptide_sequence, charge) tuples, so those three columns form the composite row key. Row order doesn't matter because this is a set comparison, so a permutation check is on. Sorting by the key is only a convenience. Protein_accession is mapped but not used as a key, because it can differ for shared peptides. Caveat on peptide format: reference peptide_sequence embeds mod names inline (e.g. DC(Carbamidomethyl)KPSEAEK). The candidate's peptide_sequence is the bare sequence. Its modified_peptide column uses mass-delta notation with flanking residues (K.LTGM[15.9949]AFR.V) and doesn't show static mods. Neither candidate column will exactly match modified reference peptides as plain strings. peptide_sequence is mapped because it matches the unmodified peptides exactly. Modified ones will need normalisation or will show as mismatches. The candidate also looks like it searched a different database (bovine/rabbit accessions vs the reference's SORC5), so little overlap is expected.

column_configs.name: protein_accession
column_configs.reasoning: The guideline says protein_accession may differ for shared peptides. The candidate preview also shows NaN for this column, so it likely reports proteins in another field. The real test is the match of the (spectrum_id, peptide_sequence, charge) ID tuples, which alignment already handles.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: The guideline says to score on whether the set of (spectrum_id, peptide_sequence, charge) tuples matches the reference. These are the ID columns used for alignment, so that match is already measured by the alignment step. Modification notation is part of peptide_sequence (for example c(carbamidomethyl) and m(oxidation)), so it is also checked through alignment. The only data column left is protein_accession, and the guideline says it may differ for shared peptides. The preview also shows NaN for it in the candidate, so the candidate seems to report proteins in another field (perhaps protein_name). Scoring protein_accession would penalise differences the task allows, so it is ignored. Extra candidate-only columns (xcorr, e_value, q_value and others) have no reference counterpart and are not compared.

notes: Scored by overlap of row keys (F1)
